mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with rising corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months where PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals an overheating labor market that typically precedes corporate profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months following two consecutive months with UNRATE below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a monetary tightening coinciding with economic contraction, which historically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rising and INDPRO falling) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of instances over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS has been above 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,400,000 units signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when HOUST exceeds 1,400,000 units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO falls below 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 370,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when RSAFS exceeds 370,000 million dollars.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months following a FEDFUNDS increase of more than 0.5pp.
